summary.text: Brandon Gill is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 26th District. A Dartmouth graduate who worked in investment banking and as a hedge fund analyst, he founded the DC Enquirer news outlet before winning the 2024 Republican primary and general election. He serves on the Judiciary, Budget and Oversight committees and is seeking a second term.

paragraphs.text: Gill was born in Clovis, New Mexico, in 1994. According to his official biography he was born on a military air force base and raised on a cattle ranch in West Texas, while Ballotpedia says he grew up outside Abilene.

He graduated cum laude from Dartmouth College in 2016 with degrees in economics and history, and his official biography says he was president of The Dartmouth Review, the student newspaper, and led the Christian Union campus ministry.

Gill began his career in finance as an investment banker and later as an analyst at a hedge fund, according to his official biography. He left finance to start the DC Enquirer, which that biography describes as an America First news outlet, and Ballotpedia also lists film producer among his career experience.

Gill won the March 5, 2024 Republican primary for the open 26th District seat with 58.4% of the vote in a field of more than ten candidates, then won the November 2024 general election with 62.1%, defeating Democrat Ernest Lineberger III and Libertarian Phil Gray.

He took office January 3, 2025. Ballotpedia lists his 2025–2026 committee assignments as Oversight and Government Reform, Judiciary and Budget, and his official biography says he serves on Judiciary, Budget and Oversight, including the DOGE Subcommittee.
Gill advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, in which he defeated Robert Chick, and is on the November ballot for a second term.
According to his official biography, he is married to Danielle D'Souza Gill, an author, and they live in Flower Mound, Texas, with their two children.
